title: The transcript vests the executive power in a president with a four-year term
summary: He is commander in chief of the army and navy, and of the militia when called into actual service. He may grant reprieves and pardons except in cases of impeachment.
body: The National Archives transcript says the executive power shall be vested in a President of the United States of America. He shall hold office during the term of four years, and, together with the Vice President, chosen for the same term, be elected as follows. A later clause says the President shall be commander in chief of the army and navy of the United States, and of the militia of the several states when called into the actual service of the United States. He may require the opinion, in writing, of the principal officer in each of the executive departments. He shall have power to grant reprieves and pardons for offences against the United States, except in cases of impeachment. The election method that follows 'as follows' is not copied in this card.

sources.title: The Constitution of the United States: A Transcription
sources.author: U.S. National Archives
sources.note: Transcription opened 2026-11-18. The card quotes the transcript. It does not add a later political reading unless a second opened page says it.
